scenes.title: Magnification Calculations
scenes.narration: Magnification Calculations. Learn how to use a light microscope and calculate magnification from image and actual sizes.

scenes.title: Cells and Microscopes
scenes.narration:
Cells and Microscopes.

Light microscopes use lenses to magnify small objects. You can see cells, tissues, and their structures clearly.

scenes.title: Microscope Views
scenes.narration:
Microscope Views.

When you look through the eyepiece you see a micrograph—the magnified image. Different specimens show different cell types.

scenes.title: The Magnification Formula
scenes.narration:
The Magnification Formula.

Magnification equals image size divided by actual size. Remember this for your exam.

scenes.title: The IAM Triangle
scenes.narration:
The IAM Triangle.

Use the triangle to remember: Image = Magnification × Actual size. Cover the one you want to find.

scenes.title: Worked Example: Plant Cell
scenes.narration:
Worked Example: Plant Cell.

A plant cell is magnified. The image is 12 mm wide. The actual cell is 0.03 mm. Find the magnification.

scenes.title: Measuring the Image
scenes.narration:
Measuring the Image.

Use a ruler to measure the image size on the photograph or screen. Convert to millimetres for the formula.

scenes.title: Worked Example Answer
scenes.narration:
Worked Example Answer.

Magnification = 12 mm ÷ 0.03 mm = 400×. Always give your answer as a number with × or 'times'.

scenes.title: Exam-Style Question
scenes.narration:
Exam-Style Question.

A root hair cell image measures 8 mm. The actual cell is 0.04 mm long. Calculate the magnification.

scenes.title: Exam-Style Answer
scenes.narration:
Exam-Style Answer.

Magnification = 8 ÷ 0.04 = 200×. Check units: both in mm, so they cancel. Always show your working.

scenes.title: Summary
scenes.narration:
Summary.

Remember: magnification = image size ÷ actual size. Use the IAM triangle to rearrange. Show units and working in your answers.
